title: 0204 - the S-at-zeros object identity is machine-checked in-tree (W2SAtZeros): the 0201/0202 DN census IS S(gamma) at the zeros (S = DN - 1/8 + O(1/T)); first in-tree |S|-at-the-zeros bound |S| <= 2.490066528 (certified 3e10 domain); flank fit shows the ladder is NOT O(1)-flat and NOT sqrt(loglog)-shaped (shape ~ ln t/loglog t); frontier pinned: Selberg CLT is generic-tau, Bondarenko-Seip omega is generic-t (RH), E19 gap-transfer fails - hA1 stays open, now characterized from three angles
body: The E19 plan named the first move on the open A1 clause (absolute O(1) for S at the zeros) as a zero-scale distribution/transfer theorem. 0204 executed the executable part of it. (1) OBJECT IDENTITY, MACHINE-CHECKED: Riemann-von Mangoldt N(T) = (T/2pi)log(T/2pi) - T/2pi + 7/8 + S(T) + O(1/T) (CITED, standard) vs the project RVM asymptotic +3/4 used by the 0201/0202 census and W2T.DN: the main terms differ by exactly 7/8 - 3/4 = 1/8, so S(T) = DN(T) - 1/8 + O(1/T) (the O(1/T) CITED, < 1e-9 for T >= 1e9). New module formal/RhAttack/W2SAtZeros.lean (root-imported): rvmShiftCore (exact, proven), sDefect_le_dnPlusShift (|DN| <= K => |S| <= K + 1/8, proven), instDnBoundToSBound_3e10 (in-tree K = 262/100 => |S| <= 549/200 = 2.745 on the certified 3e10 domain), instSignedExtremaToSBound_3e10 (with the signed measured extrema max DN = +2.615066528, min DN = -1.391662598: S range [-1.516662598, +2.490066528], hence the sharper |S| <= 2.490066528). Builds: targeted 8706 / full tree 17452 green. This is the first machine-checked in-tree |S|-at-the-zeros boundedness statement - the data-side instance of hA1, exactly in the W2Beyond4 footing (data feeds the record; proofs separate). (2) GROWTH-FORM FLANK (tmp/a1_sat_zeros_growth_fit.py): S-at-zeros running-max ladder 1.9851 (1e7) -> 2.4901 (3e10), 8 points. Fits c*ln t + b, c = 0.0628, b = 0.997 (R^2 = 0.986). Decisive diagnostic: S/ln t drifts -16.2% (0.123 -> 0.103) vs -33% for O(1)-flat, -12.8% for ln t/loglog t, -28.5% for sqrt(loglog t); sqrt(loglog t) pure-proportional under-predicts the top by -14.7% (2.124 vs 2.490); the RH main-term scale (1/4) ln t/loglog t = 1.895 at 3e10 sits below the measured 2.490. Reading: the data to 3e10 does NOT support the O(1)-at-zeros clause; the shape is closest to ln t/loglog t (RH main-term), clearly not the flatter sqrt(loglog) CLT shape; 8 points over 1.4 decades in ln t cannot yet separate slow O(1) saturation from slow divergence - the next discriminating test is a higher-T census of dS/d(ln t). (3) FRONTIER PINNED (online-verified 2026-10-28, fetch-and-identity-checked): Selberg's CLT (1946) is a GENERIC-TAU statement (tau uniform in [T,2T]) about log zeta = log|zeta| + i pi S(tau) - NOT a zeros statement (the 2024-26 follow-ups arXiv 2507.04150 / 2403.19803 / 2202.06799 all state the generic-tau form); Bondarenko-Seip (arXiv 1704.06158, Math. Ann.) gives under RH max|S(t)| >= c sqrt(log T logloglog T/loglog T) on [T^beta, T] - a generic-t omega with no zeros-vs-generic location claim; E19's gap-transfer to the zeros fails (CCM increment bound swallows the omega). So hA1 remains OPEN - now characterized from three angles at once (object identity in-tree, data shape measured, known omegas shown non-transferring). No RH claim: W2SAtZeros is a flank record on the data side of the A1 input; it does not close the clause and is not an RH face. The named open theorem is unchanged: the data-free uniform-in-frontier |DN| <= K (equivalently |S| <= K + 1/8 at the zeros), whose target shape the 0204 flank now measures directly.
